output.title: GridFrame: Layout-First Design Tool
output.tagline: Turn wireframes into responsive CSS Grid
output.description_short: Design responsive layouts that export clean CSS Grid and Flexbox — no absolute positioning, no handoff bugs.
output.description_long:
GridFrame is a layout-first design tool for product designers and design engineers who are tired of handoff friction. Sketch rough frames, and GridFrame resolves them into responsive grid systems with proper breakpoints, then exports clean, maintainable CSS Grid and Flexbox — no absolute positioning, ever.

Unlike traditional tools that output fragile, pixel-perfect rectangles, GridFrame focuses on the structural layer that engineers actually need. It audits your designs for overflow and breakpoint bugs *before* handoff, catching issues early and saving sprint time.

Perfect for startups launching a responsive redesign or building a design system, GridFrame ensures your layouts ship as intended — not rebuilt from scratch. Trusted by 3,400+ designers on the waitlist, and proven to catch real bugs: our layout audit flagged 140+ overflow issues across alpha users’ production sites.

Export code that passes stylelint with zero warnings. Build once, ship confidently.
screenshot_order: 1st: Side-by-side layout canvas and live CSS Grid export — shows structure-to-code fidelity
2nd: Layout audit panel highlighting overflow and breakpoint issues — proves proactive bug detection
3rd: Responsive preview across breakpoints — demonstrates true adaptive behavior

faq.q: How is this different from Figma?
faq.a: Figma outputs absolute rectangles; GridFrame builds responsive grid systems and exports clean CSS Grid/Flexbox engineers can use directly.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Figma designs?
faq.a: Not yet — we're focused on layout-first creation. Figma import is planned for post-alpha.

faq.q: Do you offer a free trial or sandbox?
faq.a: Not currently — we're in private alpha. Join the waitlist for early access.
Real-time co-editing is in development. Current alpha supports solo layout prototyping and export.
Yes — all demo exports pass stylelint with zero warnings. Clean, maintainable, and engineer-approved.

output.cta: Join the waitlist to build layouts that ship — not rectangles that lie.

confidence.notes: Strong product narrative and clear differentiators. All proof points are grounded in alpha feedback and technical validation.
